raj: Heads-up — running into a weird Next.js middleware/Edge runtime issue when using the JS SDK in ESM mode. On Vercel Edge the outgoing fetch to our model endpoint drains the ReadableStream and a retry path fails because the body is already consumed.

olivia: Ugh yeah that's the stream-clone thing. Edge Runtimes don't support stream.tee in some Node polyfills. What does the SDK do for retries today?

raj: It reuses the original Request body for retries. That works in node but not on the Edge because request.body is a locked stream after first use. Example minimal repro:

raj: ```js
export const config = { runtime: 'edge' }
export default async function middleware(req) {
  // using @redwood-inference/sdk pseudo API
  const res = await Redwood.generate(req.body) // consumes the stream
  // if SDK retries internally, second attempt throws "body used"
}
```

michael: We saw this in a sample app too. Workarounds I've used: clone the body manually (if readable) or buffer on the middleware and pass a freshly created Request to the SDK. Not ideal for large bodies.

olivia: Could the SDK detect Edge runtime and switch to a text/buffer fallback for smaller bodies? Or expose a hook to provide a factory that returns a fresh body per attempt?

raj: Exactly. I hacked a local patch where the SDK accepts a `bodyFactory: () => BodyInit` option and it fixed retries for our middleware. But we need a proper DX-friendly fix.

ci-bot: CI pipeline: lint, typecheck, unit-tests — started for branch fix/mw-edge-body-factory 

michael: Types note: in ESM the types for fetch's RequestInit.body differ between runtimes. We should widen the SDK typing to allow ReadableStream | BodyInit | () => BodyInit. That keeps TS happy in Next middleware projects.

sylvie: To avoid forcing buffering in every middleware, docs should show two patterns: 1) buffer-on-demand (show code that only buffers if SDK signals a retry) and 2) provide bodyFactory hooking into the SDK for streaming-safe retries. Also include Next.js-specific example with export const config = { runtime: 'edge' }.

olivia: Can someone open an RFC PR? Minimal change: add optional `bodyFactory` param + update docs + add small E2E in the edge sample app. I'll take docs.

raj: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/204 — includes tests that run in the edge sample harness (mocked ReadableStream). Left a TODO to consider automatic buffer fallback controlled by a new env flag.

michael: Thx. I added a unit test for the ESM types and one for the bodyFactory shape. CI shows one flaky in playwright for the sample app on Windows agent, rerunning. :spinner:

ci-bot: CI pipeline: rerun requested by michael — job 4572 restarted.

olivia: We should also add a short blurb in the onboarding quickstart for Next.js users: "If you deploy to Vercel Edge, prefer bodyFactory pattern or buffer small bodies; avoid attempting to reuse Request.body across retries."

raj: Agreed. Also add a short troubleshooting note: "Errors mentioning 'Failed to construct Request' or 'Cannot clone a locked stream' likely indicate Edge stream consumption during retry."

sylvie: Marking as docs + sdk fix. I'll coordinate with release notes for next patch. :memo:

raj: Thanks everyone — deploying test patch to our staging edge sample now. Will report back if anything else pops up.
